recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: The work done by the NET force acting on a
body is equal to the change in the kinetic
steps.why: The word NET carries the whole theorem: with more than one force acting, the work of any single one of them is not the change in kinetic energy.
common_mistakes: Dropping the word "net" and saying "the work done by a force", which is false whenever two forces act.

recall.must_convey: That the work done by the net force equals the change in kinetic energy.
accept: work done by the net force
equals the change in kinetic energy

steps.label: In symbols

lines.text: W = K_f − K_i = ½ m v² − ½ m u²

lines: A positive W speeds the body up; a negative
W, such as the work of friction, slows it.
steps.why: The sign of the work is the sign of the speed change, which is why friction always writes as a negative work.
common_mistakes: Writing K_i − K_f, which reverses the sign of every answer.

recall.must_convey: That W equals K final minus K initial, that is half m v squared minus half m u squared.
accept: half m v squared minus half m u squared
reject: work done by the net force
